definitions.explanation: The number four. This reading (よん) is more commonly used in modern Japanese than し because し sounds like {死|し} (death). よん is generally preferred when counting and in most compound numbers.

examples.japanese: {四|よん}⟦{人|にん}→〜人：00658_nin⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{食事|しょくじ}→食事：02087_shokuji⟧⟦しました→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: We had a meal with four people.

examples.japanese: ⟦りんご→りんご：02269_ringo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{四|よっ}つ→四つ：03039_yottsu⟧⟦あります→ある：00006_aru⟧。

⟦{一|いち}→一：00705_ichi⟧⟦{週間|しゅうかん}→週間：00988_shuukan⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{七|なな}→七：00734_nana⟧⟦{日|にち}→日：12732_nichi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦{一|いっ}→一：00705_ichi⟧⟦か{月|げつ}→ヶ月：00956_kagetsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{四|よん}⟦{週間|しゅうかん}→週間：00988_shuukan⟧⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。
examples.english: One week has seven days, and one month has four weeks.
My family has four people: my father, mother, older sister, and me.

notes:
Japanese has two main readings for four: よん and し.

PRONUNCIATION:
- よん: the most common reading, preferred in counting and compound numbers
- し: used in set expressions, but avoided in many contexts because it sounds like ⟦{死|し}→死：13248_shi⟧ (death)
- よ: appears in {四人|よにん} (four people) and some other counters

SET EXPRESSIONS USING し:
- ⟦{四月|しがつ}→四月：00668_shigatsu⟧: April
- ⟦{四季|しき}→四季：11809_shiki⟧: the four seasons
- ⟦{四角|しかく}→四角：02836_shikaku⟧: square, rectangle
- ⟦{四国|しこく}→四国：21447_shikoku⟧: Shikoku (island name)

COUNTING PATTERNS:
- ⟦{四|よっ}つ→四つ：03039_yottsu⟧: four (native Japanese counter)
- {四十|よんじゅう}: forty
- {四百|よんひゃく}: four hundred

CULTURAL NOTE:
The number four is considered unlucky (⟦{忌|い}み{数|かず}→忌み数：noentry⟧) in Japan due to the し/⟦{死|し}→死：13248_shi⟧ association. Some buildings skip the fourth floor, and sets of four are avoided as gifts.
